newsitem.title: USA: Toy Biz sees sales hurt by Marvel bankruptcy.
newsitem.headline: Toy Biz sees sales hurt by Marvel bankruptcy.

text.p: Toy Biz Inc said it believes sales of its products have been and will continue to be hurt by concerns among retailers as to the impact of Marvel Entertainment Group's bankruptcy on the future of the Toy Biz and Marvel brand.

Toy Biz said a significant portion of its revenue is derived from sales of products based on characters owned by Marvel Entertainment under an agreement with the company. Marvel filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on December 27.

On March 7, Andrews Group Inc informed Toy Biz that it did not expect to complete its previously announced merger with Toy Biz because it had terminated an agreement to purchase new shares of Marvel as part of Marvel's reorganization plan.

Marvel also announced March 7 that it had received a proposal for an equity investment from the Marvel Holding companies Bondholders' Committee as part of a new plan of reorganization and that Marvel had authorized management to work with bondholders to conduct due diligence and definitive documentation.

Representatives of the bondholders have publicly stated that they might seek to have Marvel reject the agreement under which the company manufactures and sells products based on Marvel characters. Toy Biz said that Marvel has no right to reject this agreement as a matter of law and will vigorously oppose any such action.
